## Introduction
This report finds the longest and shorted lived presidents based on how many days they lived which can be seen in the tables below. The methodology used includes both a table for longest lived presidents, including and excluding current living presidents. The only different between the two is the inclusion of Joe Biden in the longest-lived list. It then finds the statistical summary of the data then plots the data into a histogram.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = FALSE,
  warning = FALSE,
  message = FALSE,
  fig.align = "center"
)

library(lubridate)
library(gt)
library(DescTools)
```

```{r}
#imports all of the data
presidents <- read.csv("presidential_data.csv") 
president_name <- presidents$name
birth_date <- mdy(presidents$birth)
death_date <- mdy(presidents$death)

#creates the needed data
year_of_birth <- year(birth_date)
lived_days <- as.integer(death_date - birth_date)
lived_months <- lived_days/30.44
lived_years <- year(death_date) - year(birth_date)

#finds the longest and shortest lived presidents
df <- data.frame(president_name, lived_days)
longest <- df[order(-df$lived_days),][1:10,]
# longest
shortest <- df[order(df$lived_days),][1:10,]
# shortest
```

```{r}
#repeats for current living presidents
death_date_l <- replace(death_date, is.na(death_date), Sys.Date())
lived_days_l <- as.integer(death_date_l - birth_date)
df_l <- data.frame(president_name, lived_days_l)
longest_l <- df_l[order(-df_l$lived_days_l),][1:10,]
shortest_l <- df_l[order(df_l$lived_days_l),][1:10,]
```

\newpage
```{r}
#makes a table of the longest living presidents
longest |> 
  gt() |>
  tab_header(
    title = md("**Longest Lived Presidents**"),
    subtitle = md("(Excludes Living)")
  ) |>
  
  cols_label(
    president_name = "President",
    lived_days = "Days Lived"
  )|>
  tab_options(
    heading.title.font.size = "large",
    heading.subtitle.font.size = "small",
    latex.use_longtable = TRUE
  )
```

```{r}
#finds the statistical summaries of the data
#there is no mode and weighted average does not make sense in this context so they have been excluded
mean_lived = mean(lived_days, na.rm = TRUE)
median_lived = median(lived_days, na.rm = TRUE)
# mode_lived = Mode(lived_days, na.rm = TRUE)
max_lived = max(lived_days, na.rm = TRUE)
min_lived = min(lived_days, na.rm = TRUE)
sd_lived = SD(lived_days, na.rm = TRUE)

#makesa data frame of the data
summary <- data.frame(stats = c("Mean", 
                                "Median", 
                                "Maximum", 
                                "Minimum", 
                                "Standard Deviation"), 
                      vals = c( mean_lived, 
                                median_lived, 
                                max_lived, 
                                min_lived, 
                                sd_lived))

#creates a table of the statistic sums
summary |> gt() |>
  tab_header(
    title = md("**President Statistics**"),
    subtitle = md("(Based on Lived Days)")
  )|>
  cols_label(
    stats = "Statistic",
    vals = "Value"
  )|>
  tab_options(
    heading.title.font.size = "large",
    latex.use_longtable = TRUE
  )
```

```{r}
#makes a histogram
hist(lived_days[!is.na(lived_days)],
      main = "Histogram of Presidential Lifespan",
      xlab = "Days Lived")

#plots the mean and the median
abline(v = mean_lived,   col = "blue",  lwd = 3)
abline(v = median_lived,   col = "red",  lwd = 3)

#makes a legend of the data
legend("topright",
       legend = c("Mean", "Median"),
       col = c("blue", "red"),
       lwd = 3,
       cex = 0.7)
```

## Conclusion
Based on the conclusions found in the report, the longest lived president is Jimmy Carter and the shortest is John F. Kennedy. The data also appears to the skewed to the right based on both the histogram as well as the mean being higher than the median.
